sentences.zh: 三月，禮儀使上言：「東都太廟闕木主，請造以祔。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Commissioner of Rites memorialized: "The Eastern Capital Grand Ancestral Temple lacks wooden spirit tablets; we request they be made for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: the Commissioner of Rites reported that the Eastern Capital Grand Temple had no wooden spirit tablets and asked that they be made and enshrined.

sentences.zh: 」初，武后於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Initially, Empress Wu had established three temples at the Eastern Capital to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Earlier, Wu Zetian had built three temples at Luoyang—to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 至中宗已後，兩京太廟，四時並饗。

translations.literal: From Zhongzong onward, the Grand Temples of both capitals received seasonal offerings alike.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhongzong on, both capitals' Grand Temples were fed in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 至德亂後，木主多亡缺未祔。

translations.literal: After the Rebellion of Zhide, many wooden tablets were lost or missing and had not been enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Lushan rebellion, many tablets were lost or never re-enshrined.

sentences.zh: 於是議者紛然，而大旨有三：「其一曰，必存其廟，遍立群主，時饗之。

translations.literal: Then the debaters were many, but the main thrusts were three: "The first says that the temples must be preserved, spirit-lord tablets established throughout, and offerings made seasonally.
translations.idiomatic: Debate swelled, but three positions dominated: keep the temples, set up spirit-lords everywhere, and offer seasonally.

sentences.zh: 其二曰，建廟立主，存而不祭，若皇輿時巡，則就饗焉。

translations.literal: The second says to build temples and set up tablets but preserve them without sacrifice; when the imperial carriage tours, offerings are made on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Second: build temples and tablets but do not sacrifice to them—when the emperor toured, he would offer on site.

sentences.zh: 其三曰，存其廟，瘞其主，駕或東幸，則飾齋車奉京師群廟之主以往。

translations.literal: The third says to preserve the temples, bury the tablets, and when the carriage tours east, adorn the fasting carriage and convey the spirit tablets of the capital's collective temples thither.
translations.idiomatic: Third: keep the temples, bury the tablets, and on an eastern tour load the capital's tablets onto the fasting carriage and carry them east.

sentences.zh: 」議者皆不決而罷。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The debaters all could not decide and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. No faction prevailed, and the question lapsed.

sentences.zh: 四月，膳部郎中歸崇敬上疏：

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Gui Chongjian, Bureau Director in the Provisioners Bureau, submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Gui Chongjian, Director in the Provisioners Bureau, submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 二月，分司官庫部員外郎李渤奏：「太微宮神主，請歸祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Bo, Vice-Director of the Treasury in the eastern division, memorialized: "The spirit tablets of the Taiwei Palace should be returned for enshrinement in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Li Bo, eastern-division Vice-Director of the Treasury, had written that the Taiwei Palace tablets should return to the Grand Temple for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 」敕付東都留守鄭絪商量聞奏。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The edict was handed to Dongdu Resident Commissioner Zheng Yin to deliberate and report.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. An edict sent the matter to Eastern Capital Resident Commissioner Zheng Yin for deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 絪奏云：

translations.literal: Yin memorialized as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied:

sentences.zh: 敕付所司。

translations.literal: The edict was handed to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王彥威等奏議曰：

translations.literal: Wang Yanwei and other Masters of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted a deliberation:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanwei and other Court of Sacrifices Masters of Rites submitted a deliberation.

sentences.zh: 至是下尚書省集議，而郎吏所議，與彥威多同。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was sent down to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation, and what the clerks debated largely agreed with Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then convened a joint review; the clerks' views largely matched Yanwei's.

sentences.zh: 丞郎則各執所見，或曰「神主合藏于太微宮」；

translations.literal: The vice-directors and directors each held to their views; some said "the spirit tablets should jointly be stored in the Taiwei Palace";
translations.idiomatic: Directors and vice-directors split: some said the tablets should stay together in the Taiwei Palace;

sentences.zh: 或云「併合埋瘞」；

translations.literal: some said "they should together be buried and interred";
translations.idiomatic: some that they should all be buried;

sentences.zh: 或云「闕主當作」；

translations.literal: some said "missing tablets should be made";
translations.idiomatic: some that missing tablets should be carved anew;

sentences.zh: 或云「輿駕東幸，即載上都神主而東」。

translations.literal: some said "when the carriage tours east, carry the capital's spirit tablets east with it."
translations.idiomatic: some that on an eastern tour the capital's tablets should ride east with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 咸以意言，不本經據。

translations.literal: All spoke from opinion, not grounded in canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone argued from convenience, not from the classics.

sentences.zh: 竟以紛議不定，遂不舉行。

translations.literal: In the end, because discussion was unsettled, nothing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Debate deadlocked, and nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 八月，中書門下奏：「東都太廟九室神主，共二十六座，自祿山叛後，取太廟為軍營，神主棄於街巷，所司潛收聚，見在太微宮內新造小屋之內。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Secretariat memorialized: "The Eastern Capital Grand Temple's nine chambers have twenty-six spirit tablets in all; since An Lushan's rebellion, the Grand Temple was taken as a military camp and the spirit tablets were abandoned in the lanes; the relevant offices secretly gathered them in—they are now within a newly built small house inside the Taiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: the Secretariat reported that the Eastern Capital Grand Temple's nine chambers had held twenty-six tablets; after An Lushan's revolt the temple became a barracks and tablets were left in the streets until officials quietly collected them—they now sat in a new shed inside the Taiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 其太廟屋室並在，可以修崇。

translations.literal: The Grand Temple buildings remain and can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The temple buildings still stood and could be restored.

sentences.zh: 大和中，太常博士議，以為東都不合置神主，車駕東幸，即載主而行。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era, Masters of Rites deliberated and held that the Eastern Capital should not set up spirit tablets; when the imperial carriage toured east, the tablets were carried along.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe, ritual officers had ruled that Luoyang should not keep its own tablets—that on eastern tours the emperor should carry tablets with him.

sentences.zh: 至今因循，尚未修建。

translations.literal: To the present the practice has lingered and the temple has still not been rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: That expedient had lingered; the temple was still unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 望令尚書省集公卿及禮官、學官詳議。

translations.literal: It is requested that the Department of State Affairs assemble the high ministers and ritual and academic officials for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the Secretariat to gather ministers, ritualists, and scholars for a full review.

sentences.zh: 如不要更置，須有收藏去處。

translations.literal: If they are not to be set up anew, there must be a place to store them.
translations.idiomatic: If tablets were not to be reinstalled, a proper storehouse was needed.

sentences.zh: 如合置，望以所拆大寺材木修建。

translations.literal: If they are to be set up, it is requested that timber from dismantled great temples be used to rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: If they were, timber from dismantled monasteries should fund the rebuild.

sentences.zh: 既是宗室官居守，便望令充修東都太廟使，勾當修繕。

translations.literal: Since a member of the imperial clan holds the post of eastern-resident commissioner, it is requested he be appointed Commissioner for Rebuilding the Eastern Capital Grand Temple to oversee repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because a prince held the eastern residency, he should be named commissioner to rebuild the Grand Temple and supervise repairs.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕宜依。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The edict approved and it was to be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，太常博士鄭路等奏：「東都太微宮神主二十座，去年二月二十九日禮院分析聞奏訖。

translations.literal: Third month, sixth year: Zheng Lu and other Masters of Rites memorialized: "The Eastern Capital Taiwei Palace has twenty spirit tablets; on the twenty-ninth day of the second month last year the Court of Rites analyzed and reported completion.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, third month: Zheng Lu and other Masters of Rites wrote that twenty tablets remained in the Taiwei Palace and that the Court of Rites had finished its analysis on the twenty-ninth of the second month of the prior year.

sentences.zh: 伏奉今月七日敕『』者。

translations.literal: We respectfully received this month's seventh-day edict.
translations.idiomatic: They had received this month's seventh-day edict.

sentences.zh: 臣今與學官等詳議訖，謹具分析如後：獻祖宣皇帝、宣莊皇后、懿祖光皇帝、光懿皇后、文德皇后、高宗天皇大帝、則天皇后、中宗大聖大昭孝皇帝、和思皇后、昭成皇后、孝敬皇帝、地敬哀皇后已前十二座，親盡迭毀，宜遷諸太廟，祔於興聖廟。

translations.literal: Your servants have now deliberated in detail with the academic officials and respectfully submit analysis as follows: the twelve tablets before Xianzu the Sagely Emperor, Empress Xuanzhuang, Yizu the Radiant Emperor, Empress Guangyi, Empress Wende, Emperor Gaozong the Heavenly August, Empress Zetian, Emperor Zhongzong the Great Sage and Great Filial, Empress Hexian, Empress Zhaocheng, Emperor Xiaojing, and Empress Jing'ai of the Earth—kinship exhausted in rotation—should be transferred to the various Grand Temples and enshrined at the Xingsheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After consulting scholars they proposed: twelve tablets—from Xianzu and Xuanzhuang through Yizu, Wende, Gaozong, Zetian, Zhongzong, Hexian, Zhaocheng, Xiaojing, and Jing'ai—had passed the limit of mourning and should move to the capital temples and the Xingsheng shrine.

sentences.zh: 禘祫之歲，乃一祭之。

translations.literal: In years of di and cha sacrifice, they receive a single offering together.
translations.idiomatic: In di and cha years they would receive one joint offering.

sentences.zh: 東都無興聖廟可祔，伏請且權藏於太廟夾室。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital has no Xingsheng Temple for enshrinement; we request they be provisionally stored in the side chambers of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had no Xingsheng Temple; they asked to lodge the tablets temporarily in the Grand Temple's side chambers.

sentences.zh: 未題神主十四座，前件神主既無題號之文，難伸祝告之禮。

translations.literal: Fourteen tablets lack inscriptions; as the aforesaid tablets lack inscribed text, the prayer-and-announcement rite cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen tablets bore no inscription, so the prayer of enshrinement could not be spoken.

sentences.zh: 今與禮官等商量，伏請告遷之日，但瘞於舊太微宮內空閒之地。

translations.literal: We have now deliberated with the ritual officers; we request that on the day of announcing removal they simply be interred in vacant ground within the old Taiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: With ritual officers they agreed that on the day of removal those fourteen should be buried in unused ground inside the old Taiwei compound.

sentences.zh: 恭酌事理，庶協從宜。

translations.literal: Respectfully weighing the matter, it should accord with convenience.
translations.idiomatic: That, they judged, best fit practical need.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Approved.

sentences.zh: 太常博士段瑰等三十九人奏議曰：

translations.literal: Duan Gui and thirty-nine other Masters of Rites submitted a deliberation:
translations.idiomatic: Duan Gui and thirty-nine other Masters of Rites submitted a counter-memorial.

sentences.zh: 其年九月敕：「」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year an edict:
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month an edict went out—

sentences.zh: 工部尚書薛元賞等議：

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xue Yuanshang and others deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xue Yuanshang and others replied:

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中鄭亞等五人議：「據禮院奏，以為東都太廟既廢，不可復修，見在太微宮神主，請瘞於所寓之地。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Personnel Zheng Ya and five others: "According to the Court of Rites memorial, it holds the Eastern Capital Grand Temple having been abandoned cannot be rebuilt, and the spirit tablets now in Taiwei Palace should be interred where they are housed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ya of Personnel and five colleagues: the Court of Rites had said the Eastern Capital temple was beyond repair and the Taiwei tablets should be buried where they lay.

sentences.zh: 有乖經訓，不敢雷同。

translations.literal: This deviates from canonical instruction; we dare not concur.
translations.idiomatic: That strayed from the classics; they would not sign.

sentences.zh: 臣所以別進議狀，請修祔主，並依典禮，兼與禮儀使顏真卿所奏事同。

translations.literal: Your servants therefore submitted a separate deliberation requesting repair and enshrinement of tablets, all according to canonical rites, the same as Commissioner of Rites Yan Zhenqing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: They filed a separate opinion—to restore the temple, remake and enshrine the tablets per canon, matching Yan Zhenqing's memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣與公卿等重議，皆以為廟固合修，主不可瘞，即與臣等別狀意同。

translations.literal: Your servants and the high ministers deliberated again and all held the temples should be rebuilt and tablets cannot be interred— the same as your servants' separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In renewed debate with the grandees, all agreed: rebuild the temple, do not bury the tablets—their view matched the separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 但眾議猶疑東西二廟，各設神主，恐涉廟有二主之義，請修廟虛室，乙太微宮所寓神主藏於夾室之中。

translations.literal: But collective deliberation still doubted that east and west each setting up tablets might involve the meaning of a temple having two lords; they requested rebuilding the temple with vacant chambers and storing the Taiwei housed tablets in side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many still feared two capitals each keeping tablets implied two lords in one temple; they proposed restoring empty chambers and housing the Taiwei tablets in side rooms.

sentences.zh: 伏以六主神位，內有不祧之宗，今用遷廟之儀，猶未合禮。

translations.literal: Respectfully, among the six spirit-lord positions within are unfilleted ancestors; to use relocation rites now still does not accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Six of those spirit-lords were unfilleted forebears; applying removal rites to them still seemed uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 臣等猶未敢署眾狀，蓋為闕疑。

translations.literal: Your servants still dare not sign the collective memorial, because doubts remain.
translations.idiomatic: They still refused to endorse the joint report while doubt remained.

translations.literal: The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 太學博士直弘文館鄭遂等七人議曰：「夫論國之大事，必本乎正而根乎經，以臻于中道。

translations.literal: Zheng Sui and seven others, Great Learning Masters direct in the Hongwen Pavilion: "In discussing great affairs of state, one must root them in rectitude and the classics, to reach the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sui of the Grand Academy and six Hongwen colleagues: statecraft must stand on rectitude and the classics and aim at the mean.

sentences.zh: 聖朝以廣孝為先，以得禮為貴，而臣下敢不以經對。

translations.literal: The sage dynasty takes broad filial piety first and obtaining the rites as precious—and how could ministers not answer with the classics?
translations.idiomatic: This dynasty prizes filial piety and true ritual—how could ministers answer with anything but the canon?

sentences.zh: 三論六故，已詳於前議矣。

translations.literal: The three arguments and six antecedents have already been detailed in the prior deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Three positions and six precedents had already been laid out.

sentences.zh: 再捧天問，而陳乎諸家之說，求於典訓，考乎大中，廟有必修之文，主無可置之理。

translations.literal: Again receiving Heaven's query, we set forth the various schools' theories, seeking in canonical instruction, examining the mean—temples have text requiring repair, tablets have no text permitting establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Asked again from the throne, they surveyed every school against the classics: temples must be repaired; tablets could not simply be installed.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: For what reason?

sentences.zh: 正經正史，兩都之廟可徵。

translations.literal: Orthodox classics and histories—both capitals' temples can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Because orthodox classics and histories attest temples in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 《禮》稱『天子不卜處太廟』，『擇日卜建國之地，則宗廟可知』。

translations.literal: The Rites says "the Son of Heaven does not divine the site of the Grand Temple" and "when one selects a day to divine the site for founding the state, the ancestral temples can be known."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says the Son of Heaven does not divine the Grand Temple's site, and that when he divines where to found the state, the temples are already implied.

sentences.zh: 則廢廟之說，恐非所宜廢。

translations.literal: Then the theory of abandoning temples is perhaps not what should be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon a temple, then, is what ought not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 謹按《詩》、《書》、《禮》三經及漢朝兩史，兩都並設廟，而載主之制，久已行之。

translations.literal: We respectfully note the three classics of Odes, Documents, and Rites and the two histories of Han—both capitals set up temples, and the system of enshrining tablets has long been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes, Documents, Rites, and both Han histories show both capitals with temples and long-standing tablet rites.

sentences.zh: 敢不明徵而去文飾，援據經文，不易前見，東都太廟，合務修崇，而舊主當瘞，請于太微宮所藏之所。

translations.literal: We dare clarify the evidence and set aside literary ornament; relying on canonical text, not altering prior views—the Eastern Capital Grand Temple should be restored, while old tablets should be interred at the place stored in Taiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They cited text plainly: restore the Eastern Capital Grand Temple; bury the old tablets where the Taiwei Palace had held them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝有事于洛，則奉齋車載主以行。

translations.literal: When the emperor has affairs at Luoyang, then with fasting carriage convey the tablets.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Luoyang, a fasting carriage would carry the tablets.

translations.literal: The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 太常博士顧德章議曰：

translations.literal: Gu Dezang, Master of Rites, deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dezang, Master of Rites, also submitted.

sentences.zh: 德章又有上中書門下及禮院詳議兩狀，並同載於後。

translations.literal: Dezang also had two memorials for detailed deliberation to the Secretariat and Court of Rites, both recorded below.
translations.idiomatic: Dezang filed two further opinions to the Secretariat and Court of Rites, copied below.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：

translations.literal: The first states:
translations.idiomatic: The first read:

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second states:
translations.idiomatic: The second read:

sentences.zh: 制曰：「」六年三月，擇日既定，禮官既行，旋以武宗登遐，其事遂寢。

translations.literal: The statute said: Sixth year, third month, once the day was fixed and ritual officers had proceeded, soon Wuzong passed away and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had fixed a date in the sixth year's third month; ritual officers had begun—then Wuzong died and the work slept.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，竟迎太微宮神主祔東都太廟，禘祫之禮，盡出神主合食于太祖之前。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, at last the Taiwei Palace spirit tablets were welcomed for enshrinement in the Eastern Capital Grand Temple; di and cha rites—all spirit tablets were jointly offered before the Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong at last welcomed the Taiwei tablets into the Eastern Capital Grand Temple; at di and cha all tablets were offered together before the Great Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀禮》，祫享，功臣配享于廟庭，禘享則不配。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Rites: at cha offering, meritorious subjects were paired in offering in the temple courtyard; at di offering they were not paired.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites paired meritorious subjects in the courtyard at cha, not at di.

sentences.zh: 當時令文，祫禘之日，功臣並得配享。

translations.literal: At that time the ordinance stated on cha and di days meritorious subjects all received paired offering.
translations.idiomatic: A later ordinance allowed pairing at both cha and di.

sentences.zh: ，將行禘祭，有司請集禮官學士等議，太常卿韋挺等一十八人議曰：「古之王者，富有四海，而不朝夕上膳於宗廟者，患其禮過也。

translations.literal: When a di sacrifice was about to be performed, the relevant offices requested assembling ritual and academic officials for deliberation; Wei Ting, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and eighteen others deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Before a scheduled di, the offices convened ritualists and scholars; Director Wei Ting and eighteen others argued:

sentences.zh: 故曰：『春秋祭祀，以時思之。

translations.literal: Of old kings possessed the four seas yet did not daily present upper meals at the ancestral temple, fearing excess in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings held the four seas yet did not daily feast the ancestors, lest ritual grow excessive.

sentences.zh: 』至於臣有大功享祿，其後孝子率禮，潔粢豐盛，禮、祀、烝、嘗，四時不輟，國家大祫，又得配焉。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: "Spring and autumn offerings—at the proper seasons one thinks of them."
translations.idiomatic: Hence: spring and autumn offerings—memory at the proper season.

sentences.zh: 所以昭明其勳，尊顯其德，以勸嗣臣也。

translations.literal: As for ministers with great merit enjoying emoluments, afterward filial sons observe rite with pure grain and abundant offerings—li, si, zheng, chang—uninterrupted through four seasons; at the state's great cha they could also be paired.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of great merit, once enfeoffed, received seasonal li, si, zheng, and chang from filial heirs; at the great cha the state might pair them too.

sentences.zh: 其禘及時享，功臣皆不應預。

translations.literal: Hence at di and seasonal offerings meritorious subjects all should not participate.
translations.idiomatic: But at di and ordinary seasonal rites they should not appear.

sentences.zh: 故周禮六功之官，皆配大烝而已。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou Rites officials of the six achievements are paired only at the great zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rites pairs the six grades of merit only at the great zheng.

sentences.zh: 先儒皆取大烝為祫祭。

translations.literal: Former scholars all take great zheng as cha sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars identified great zheng with cha.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆、庾蔚之等多遵鄭學，未有將為時享。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong, Yu Weizhi, and many others followed Zheng Xuan's learning; none treated it as seasonal offering.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong, Yu Weizhi, and others followed Zheng Xuan—none applied it to seasonal feasts.

sentences.zh: 又漢、魏祫祀，皆在十月，晉朝禮官，欲用孟秋殷祭，左僕射孔安國啟彈，坐免者不一。

translations.literal: Also Han and Wei cha sacrifices were all in the tenth month; Jin ritual officers wished to use the seventh month's yin offering—Left Vice Director Kong Anguo submitted remonstrance; those dismissed were not few.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei held cha in the tenth month; Jin officers wanted the seventh-month yin rite—Kong Anguo remonstrated, and many lost office.

sentences.zh: 梁初誤禘功臣，左丞何佟之駁議，武帝允而依行。

translations.literal: At Liang's beginning meritorious subjects were mistakenly paired at di; Left Assistant Censor He Tongzhi refuted—Emperor Wu approved and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Early Liang wrongly paired merit at di; He Tongzhi objected, and Emperor Wu agreed.

sentences.zh: 降洎周、齊，俱遵此禮。

translations.literal: Down through Zhou and Qi, all followed this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Qi kept the same rule.

sentences.zh: 竊以五年再殷，合諸天道，一大一小，通人雅論，小則人臣不預，大則兼及功臣。

translations.literal: We hold that the great and small yin offerings twice in five years accord with Heaven's way; one great and one small, the general human view—at the small, ministers do not participate; at the great, meritorious subjects are included.
translations.idiomatic: Twice in five years—great and small yin—matches heaven's rhythm: the small excludes ministers; the great includes merit.

sentences.zh: 今禮禘無功臣，誠謂禮不可易。

translations.literal: Now ritual: di without meritorious subjects—we hold ritual cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: To pair merit at di would break ritual—and ritual, they said, must not bend.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔改令從禮。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Thereupon an edict revised the ordinance to follow ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. An edict brought the ordinance back in line with the classics.

sentences.zh: 至開元中改修禮，復令禘祫俱以功臣配饗焉。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era when rites were revised, again di and cha both allowed meritorious subjects paired offering.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan's ritual revision again allowed merit at both di and cha.

sentences.zh: 高宗十月，將祫享於太廟。

translations.literal: Tenth month of Gaozong—about to perform cha offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's tenth month: a cha at the Grand Temple was due.

sentences.zh: 時議者以《禮緯》「三年一祫，五年一禘」、《公羊傳》云「五年而再殷祭」，議交互莫能斷決。

translations.literal: Debaters cited the Rites Weft "cha every three years, di every five" and Gongyang "great yin offerings twice in five years"—arguments crossed and none could decide.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars cited the Rites Weft—cha every three years, di every five—and Gongyang's "twice in five years"; no line prevailed.

sentences.zh: 太學博士史璨等議曰：「按《禮記正義》引鄭玄《禘祫志》云：『《春秋》：僖公三十三年十二月薨。

translations.literal: Shi Can and other Great Learning Masters: "According to Rites Records orthodox commentary citing Zheng Xuan's "Di and Cha Record": "Springs and Autumns: Duke Xi died in the thirty-third year, twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Can and academy colleagues cited Zheng Xuan's Di and Cha Record in the Rites commentary: Duke Xi of Lu died in his thirty-third year, twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 文公二年八月丁卯，大享於太廟。

translations.literal: Duke Wen's second year, eighth month, day dingmao—great offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Wen's second year, eighth month, day dingmao, a great offering at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》云：大享者何？

translations.literal: Gongyang asks: what is great offering?
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang asks: what is a great offering?

sentences.zh: 祫也。

translations.literal: Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Joint offering.

sentences.zh: 』是三年喪畢，新君二年當祫，明年當禘於群廟。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Thus three years' mourning concluded; the new lord's second year should cha, the next year di at the collective temples.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Three years' mourning done, the new ruler cha'd in year two and di'd at the group temples in year three.

sentences.zh: 僖公、宣公八年皆有禘，則後禘去前禘五年。

translations.literal: Duke Xi and Duke Xuan's eighth year both have di—so later di is five years from former di.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Xuan both di'd in year eight—five years between di rites.

sentences.zh: 以此定之，則新君二年祫，三年禘。

translations.literal: By this determination: new lord year two cha, year three di.
translations.idiomatic: So: year two cha, year three di.

sentences.zh: 自爾已後，五年而再殷祭，則六年當祫，八年當禘。

translations.literal: From then on, great yin twice in five years—year six cha, year eight di.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, twice in five years: year six cha, year eight di.

sentences.zh: 又昭公十年，齊歸薨，至十三年喪畢當祫，為平丘之會，冬，公如晉。

translations.literal: Also Duke Zhao's tenth year—Qi Gui died; year thirteen mourning concludes and should cha, but for the Pingqiu assembly—in winter the duke went to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao year ten: Qi Gui died; year thirteen should have seen cha, but the Pingqiu congress sent him to Jin that winter.

sentences.zh: 至十四年祫，十五年禘《傳》云『有事于武宮』是也。

translations.literal: Year fourteen cha, year fifteen di—the Documents says "affairs at Wugong"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: Year fourteen cha, fifteen di—the Annals' "affairs at Wugong."

sentences.zh: 至十八年祫，二十年禘。

translations.literal: Year eighteen cha, year twenty di.
translations.idiomatic: Year eighteen cha, twenty di.

sentences.zh: 二十三年祫，二十五年禘。

translations.literal: Year twenty-three cha, year twenty-five di.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-three cha, twenty-five di.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十五年『有事于襄宮』是也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's twenty-fifth year "affairs at Xiang Palace"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's twenty-fifth year—"affairs at Xiang Palace"—marks the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 如上所云，則禘已後隔三年祫，已後隔二年禘。

translations.literal: As stated above, then after di three years until xia, thereafter two years until di.
translations.idiomatic: As stated above, after a di sacrifice three years pass until xia, then two years until the next di.

sentences.zh: 此則有合禮經，不違《傳》義。

translations.literal: This accords with the ritual classics and does not violate the Commentaries' meaning.
translations.idiomatic: This fits the ritual classics and does not violate the Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 」自此依璨等議為定。

translations.literal: " From this point the proposal of Can and others was fixed as the rule.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on Can's proposal was adopted as the rule.

sentences.zh: 秋，睿宗喪畢，祫享於太廟。

translations.literal: In autumn, when Ruizong's mourning was completed, xia offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Ruizong's mourning ended, a xia offering was held at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自後又相承三年一祫，五年一禘，各自計年，不相通數。

translations.literal: Thereafter again the practice continued: xia every three years, di every five years, each counting years separately without coordinating the cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the practice again was xia every three years and di every five years, each cycle counted on its own without aligning the numbers.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年，凡經五禘、七祫。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year, there had been five di and seven xia in all.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year there had been five di and seven xia in all.

sentences.zh: 其年夏禘訖，冬又當祫。

translations.literal: That year after the summer di was finished, winter again called for xia.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after the summer di was completed, winter again required xia.

sentences.zh: 太常議曰：

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed:
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized:

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎崔宗之駁下太常，令更詳議，令集賢學士陸善經等更加詳核，善經亦以其議為允。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Rites Cui Zongzhi rejected and sent it down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, ordering further detailed discussion; ordered Hanlin academician Lu Shanqing and others to examine further; Shanqing also approved their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Rites Cui Zongzhi rejected the proposal and returned it to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for further review; Lu Shanqing and other Hanlin academicians were ordered to examine it again, and Shanqing also approved their view.

sentences.zh: 於是太常卿韋縚奏曰：「禮有禘祫，俱稱殷祭，二法更用，鱗次相承。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Can memorialized, saying: "In ritual there are di and xia, both called substantive sacrifices; the two methods alternate in use, succeeding like fish scales.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wei Can then memorialized: "Ritual provides di and xia, both called substantive sacrifices; the two rites alternate in succession like scales on a fish.

sentences.zh: 或云五歲再殷，一禘一祫。

translations.literal: Some say at five years two substantive sacrifices—one di and one xia.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that in five years there are two substantive sacrifices—one di and one xia.

sentences.zh: 或云三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: Some say xia every three years, di every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Others say xia every three years and di every five.

sentences.zh: 法天象閏，大趣皆同。

translations.literal: Following heaven's pattern and the intercalary, the great import is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Both follow heaven's pattern and the intercalary month; the underlying principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 皆以太廟禘祫，計年有差，考于經傳，微有所乖。

translations.literal: All take the Grand Temple di and xia, with years counted differently; examining the classics and commentaries, there is slight divergence.
translations.idiomatic: All concern di and xia at the Grand Temple, but the year-count differs; compared with the classics and commentaries, there is a slight discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 頃在四月，已行禘享，今指孟冬，又申祫儀，合食禮頻，恐違先典。

translations.literal: Recently in the fourth month di offering was already performed; now pointing to mid-winter, xia rites are again reported—joint offerings too frequent, fearing violation of former canons.
translations.idiomatic: Di was just performed in the fourth month; now, with mid-winter approaching, xia rites are proposed again—joint offerings would come too often and may violate ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下能事畢舉，舊物咸甄，宗祏祗慎之時，經訓申明之日。

translations.literal: We submit that Your Majesty, able affairs completed, old things all restored, when the ancestral tablets are reverently tended, when classic teachings are clarified—
translations.idiomatic: We submit that Your Majesty has completed the mourning observances, restored what was lost, and now, when the ancestral tablets are tended and the classics clarified—

sentences.zh: 臣等忝在持禮，職司討論，輒據舊文，定其倫序。

translations.literal: We humbly hold ritual office, charged with discussion, and presume to fix their order according to old texts.
translations.idiomatic: we who hold ritual office are charged with deliberation and presume to set the order according to old texts.

sentences.zh: 請以今年夏禘，便為殷祭之源，自此之後，禘、祫相代，五年再殷，周而復始。

translations.literal: Please take this year's summer di as the source of substantive sacrifices; from then on di and xia alternate, two substantive sacrifices in five years, cycling and beginning again.
translations.idiomatic: Let this year's summer di be the starting point for substantive sacrifices; thereafter di and xia should alternate, two substantive sacrifices every five years, and the cycle begin anew.

sentences.zh: 其今年冬祫，准禮合停，望令所司但行時享，即嚴禋不黷，庶合舊儀。

translations.literal: This year's winter xia per ritual should be suspended; we hope the responsible offices will only perform seasonal offerings—that is strict sacrifice without profanation, roughly matching old observances.
translations.idiomatic: This year's winter xia should be omitted per ritual; we ask that the offices perform only the seasonal offerings—strict sacrifice without excess—and thus match former practice.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: " The decree followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，閏六月六日敕文：「」

translations.literal: Former observance, intercalary sixth month sixth day edict text: ""
translations.idiomatic: Former observance: sixth day of the intercalary sixth month, edict text: ""

sentences.zh: 九月四日，太常博士陳京上疏言：

translations.literal: Fourth day of the ninth month, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor Chen Jing submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the ninth month, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor Chen Jing submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 敕下尚書省百僚集議。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the Ministry of State for all officials to assemble and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of State to assemble all officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使太子少師顏真卿議曰：「議者或云獻祖、懿祖親遠廟遷，不當祫享，宜永閟西夾室。

translations.literal: Rites Commissioner, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Yan Zhenqing proposed: "Some discussants say Xianzu and Yizu, kin distant and temples migrated, should not receive xia offering and should be permanently closed in the west side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Commissioner and Junior Tutor Yan Zhenqing proposed: "Some say that Xianzu and Yizu, being distant in kin and having had their temples moved, should not receive xia offerings and should be permanently shut in the west side chambers.

sentences.zh: 又議者云二祖宜同祫享，于太祖並昭穆，而空太祖東向之位。

translations.literal: Others say the two ancestors should share xia offering with the Grand Ancestor in zhao-mu order, leaving the Grand Ancestor's east-facing position empty.
translations.idiomatic: Others say the two ancestors should share xia with the Grand Ancestor in zhao-mu order, leaving the Grand Ancestor's east-facing seat vacant.

sentences.zh: 又議者云，二祖若同袷享，即太祖之位永不得正，宜奉遷二祖神主祔藏于德明皇帝廟。

translations.literal: Others say if the two ancestors share xia offering, the Grand Ancestor's position could never be corrected; they should enshrine the two ancestors' spirit tablets in the temple of the Virtuous and Illustrious Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Others say that if the two ancestors share xia, the Grand Ancestor's seat could never be corrected; the two ancestors' tablets should be moved to the temple of the Virtuous and Illustrious Emperor.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以三議俱未為允。

translations.literal: I submit all three proposals are not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that all three proposals are unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 且禮經殘缺，既無明據，儒者能方義類，斟酌其中，則可舉而行之，蓋協於正也。

translations.literal: The ritual classics are damaged and lack clear warrant; scholars who can compare categories and weigh among them may then act—this broadly accords with what is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual classics are damaged and lack clear authority; scholars who can compare categories and weigh the matter may act—this broadly accords with what is correct.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖景皇帝以受命始封之功，處百代不遷之廟，配天崇享，是極尊嚴。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, the Illustrious Emperor, for merit in first enfeoffment at receiving the mandate, occupies the temple never moved for a hundred generations, paired with Heaven in lofty offering—this is utmost honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Jing, for merit at first enfeoffment when the mandate was received, occupies the temple that is never moved for a hundred generations and is paired with Heaven in lofty sacrifice—this is the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 且至禘祫之時，暫居昭穆之位，屈己申孝，敬奉祖宗，緣齒族之禮，廣尊先之道，此實太祖明神烝烝之本意，亦所以化被天下，率循孝悌也。

translations.literal: When great di and xia arrive, he temporarily occupies zhao-mu position, humbling himself to extend filial piety, respectfully serving ancestors and forbears—by kinship order's rite, broadening honor of forebears; this truly is the Grand Ancestor's bright spirit's earnest intent, also thereby transforming the realm, leading all in filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At great di and xia he temporarily takes a zhao-mu place, humbling himself to extend filial piety and serve the ancestors—by the rite of kin order, broadening honor to forebears. This is truly the Grand Ancestor's intent, and thereby transforms the realm and leads all in filial piety.

sentences.zh: 請依晉蔡謨等議，至十月祫享之日奉獻祖神主居東向之位，自懿祖、太祖洎諸祖宗，遵左昭右穆之列。

translations.literal: Please follow Jin Cai Mo's proposal: on the tenth month's xia offering day present Xianzu's spirit tablet in the east-facing position; from Yizu, Grand Ancestor, down through all ancestors follow left-zhao right-mu array.
translations.idiomatic: Please follow Jin Cai Mo's proposal: on the day of the tenth month's xia offering, place Xianzu's tablet in the east-facing position; from Yizu and the Grand Ancestor down through all ancestors, follow the left-zhao right-mu array.

sentences.zh: 此有彰國家重本尚順之明義，足為萬代不易之令典也。

translations.literal: This has the clear meaning of the state weighting the root and honoring obedience—sufficient as an unchanging statute for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This clearly expresses the state's weight on the root and honoring of obedience—sufficient as an unchanging statute for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 又議者請奉二祖神主于德明皇帝廟，行祫祭之禮。

translations.literal: Others propose installing the two ancestors' spirit tablets in the Virtuous and Illustrious Emperor's temple to perform xia rites.
translations.idiomatic: Others propose placing the two ancestors' tablets in the Virtuous and Illustrious Emperor's temple to perform xia.

sentences.zh: 夫祫，合也。

translations.literal: Xia means union.
translations.idiomatic: Xia denotes union.

sentences.zh: 故《公羊傳》云：『大事者何？

translations.literal: Thus the Gongyang Commentary says: "What is a great affair?
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says: "What is a great affair?

sentences.zh: 祫也。

translations.literal: Xia."
translations.idiomatic: It is xia."

sentences.zh: 』若祫祭不陳於太廟而享於德明廟，是乃分食也，豈謂合食乎？

translations.literal: If xia sacrifice is not set out in the Grand Temple but offered in the Virtuous and Illustrious temple, this is divided offering—how can it be called joint offering?
translations.idiomatic: If xia is not performed in the Grand Temple but in the Virtuous and Illustrious temple, that is divided offering—how can it be called joint offering?

sentences.zh: 名實相乖，深失禮意，固不可行也。

translations.literal: Name and substance contradict each other, deeply losing ritual intent—certainly not executable.
translations.idiomatic: Name and substance contradict each other and deeply violate ritual intent—it certainly cannot be done.

translations.literal: The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ended.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十八日，太常卿裴郁奏曰：「禘、祫之禮，殷、周以遷廟皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month, Director Pei Yu memorialized, saying: "The rites of di and xia—in Yin and Zhou, because moved temples all came after the Grand Ancestor, joint offering could be ordered and honor and subordination did not err.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth of the eleventh month, Director Pei Yu memorialized: "Di and xia—in Yin and Zhou, because moved temples all came after the Grand Ancestor, joint offerings could be ordered without confusion of rank.

sentences.zh: 及漢高受命，無始封祖，以高皇帝為太祖。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu received the mandate, there was no founding enfeoffment ancestor; the High Emperor was taken as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu received the mandate there was no founding enfeoffment ancestor; the High Emperor was made Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太上皇，高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Emperor, the High Emperor's father, had a temple established for offering—he was not in the zhao-mu joint-offering array, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Emperor, Gaozu's father, had a temple for sacrifice but was not in the zhao-mu joint-offering order, being honored above the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。

translations.literal: Wei Wu founded the enterprise; Emperor Wen received the mandate and likewise took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao founded the enterprise; Emperor Wen received the mandate and likewise took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 其高皇、太皇、處士君等，並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。

translations.literal: The High Emperor, Supreme Emperor, Recluse Lord, and others were all subordinate in honor and not in the zhao-mu joint-offering array.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor, Supreme Emperor, Recluse Lord, and others were all subordinate in honor and outside the zhao-mu joint-offering order.

sentences.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。

translations.literal: Jin Xuan founded the enterprise; Emperor Wu received the mandate and likewise took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi founded the enterprise; Emperor Wu received the mandate and likewise took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 其征西、潁川等四府君，亦為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。

translations.literal: The Western Campaign, Yingchuan, and other four mansion lords were also subordinate in honor and not in the zhao-mu joint-offering array.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Campaign, Yingchuan, and other four mansion lords were likewise subordinate in honor and outside the zhao-mu joint-offering order.

sentences.zh: 國家誕受天命，累聖重光。

translations.literal: Our state received the Mandate of Heaven; successive sages doubled its glory.
translations.idiomatic: Our state received the Mandate of Heaven; successive sage rulers doubled its glory.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing first received enfeoffment as Duke of Tang and truly was Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing was first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang and was truly the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 中間世數既近，於三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，惟有六室。

translations.literal: The generations in between were near; within the three zhao and three mu, the royal Grand Temple therefore had only six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The intervening generations were few; within the three zhao and three mu, the imperial Grand Temple therefore had only six chambers.

sentences.zh: 其弘農府君、宣、光二祖，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆之數。

translations.literal: The Lord of Hongnong Mansion, the two ancestors Xuan and Guang, honored above the Grand Ancestor—when kin was exhausted they moved temples and were not counted in zhao-mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Hongnong Mansion and the two ancestors Xuan and Guang, honored above the Grand Ancestor—when kin was exhausted their temples were moved and they were not counted in zhao-mu.

sentences.zh: 著在禮志，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Recorded in the ritual annals; it may be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: This is recorded in the ritual annals and may be followed.

sentences.zh: 開元中，加置九廟，獻、懿二祖皆在昭穆，是以太祖景皇帝未得居東向之尊。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era nine temple chambers were added; the two ancestors of Offerings and Eminence were both in zhao-mu, so the Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing could not occupy the east-facing honor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan nine chambers were added; Offerings and Eminence were both in zhao-mu, so Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing could not take the east-facing honor.

sentences.zh: 今二祖已祧，九室惟序，則太祖之位又安可不正？

translations.literal: Now the two ancestors have been moved out; with nine chambers in order only, how can the Grand Ancestor's position again not be corrected?
translations.idiomatic: Now the two ancestors have been moved out and the nine chambers are in order—how can the Grand Ancestor's seat again fail to be corrected?

sentences.zh: 伏乙太祖上配天地，百代不遷，而居昭穆，獻、懿二祖，親盡廟遷，而居東向，徵諸故實，實所未安。

translations.literal: We submit that the Grand Ancestor, paired above with Heaven and Earth, never moved for a hundred generations, yet occupies zhao-mu, while the two ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, kin exhausted and temples moved, occupy the east-facing—examining former facts, this is truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that the Grand Ancestor, paired with Heaven and Earth and never moved for a hundred generations, yet occupies zhao-mu, while Offerings and Eminence, kin exhausted and temples moved, occupy the east-facing—examining precedent, this is truly improper.

sentences.zh: 請下百僚僉議。

translations.literal: We ask that all officials be ordered to deliberate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that all officials deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨依。

translations.literal: " The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 八年正月二十三日，太子左庶子李嶸等七人議曰：

translations.literal: Twenty-third day of the first month of the eighth year, Left Associate of the Heir Apparent Li Rong and seven others proposed:
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third of the first month of the eighth year, Left Associate of the Heir Apparent Li Rong and seven others proposed:

translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian of Personnel and eleven others proposed:

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian of Works and others proposed:

translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu of the Bureau of Merits proposed:

translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing of the Bureau of Evaluation proposed:

translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ziling, magistrate of Tongguan, proposed:

sentences.zh: 其月二十七日，吏部郎中柳冕上《禘祫義證》，凡一十四道，以備顧問，並議奏聞。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh of that month, Director of the Ministry of Personnel Liu Mian submitted "Evidence on Di and Xia," fourteen items in all, for consultation, and all were deliberated and reported.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of that month, Liu Mian submitted "Evidence on Di and Xia," fourteen items in all, for consultation; all were deliberated and reported.

sentences.zh: 至三月十二日，祠部奏郁等議狀。

translations.literal: By the twelfth day of the third month, the Bureau of Sacrifices reported Yu and others' deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth of the third month, the Bureau of Sacrifices reported Yu and others' deliberation.

sentences.zh: 至十一年七月十二日，敕：「」其月二十六日，左司郎中陸淳奏曰：「臣尋七年百僚所議，雖有一十六狀，總其歸趣，三端而已。

translations.literal: By the twelfth day of the seventh month of the eleventh year, an edict: "" That month on the twenty-sixth, Left Bureau Director Lu Chun memorialized, saying: "Your subject traced the seventh-year deliberation of all officials—though there were sixteen memorials in all, their trend has three points only.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth of the seventh month of the eleventh year, an edict: "" That month on the twenty-sixth, Left Bureau Director Lu Chun memorialized: "Your subject reviewed the seventh-year deliberation of all officials—though there were sixteen memorials, their trend has three points only.

sentences.zh: 于頎等一十四狀，並云復太祖之位。

translations.literal: Yu Hao and others' fourteen memorials all said to restore the Grand Ancestor's position.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hao and others' fourteen memorials all said to restore the Grand Ancestor's seat.

sentences.zh: 張薦狀則云並列昭穆，而虛東饗之位。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian's memorial said to array both in zhao-mu and leave the east-facing seat empty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian argued for zhao-mu placement with an empty east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 韋武狀同云當祫之歲，獻祖居於東向，行禘之禮，太祖復筵于西。

translations.literal: Wei Wu's memorial likewise said that in the year of xia, Xianzu should occupy the east-facing and perform di rites; the Grand Ancestor should again take his place in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu's memorial likewise said that in a xia year Xianzu should face east and perform di, while the Grand Ancestor should again take the western seat.

sentences.zh: 謹按禮經及先儒之說，復太祖之位，位既正也，義在不疑。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the ritual classics and former scholars' explanations, to restore the Grand Ancestor's position—the position once corrected, the meaning admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: According to the ritual classics and former scholars, restoring the Grand Ancestor's seat—once the seat is corrected, the meaning admits no doubt.

sentences.zh: 太祖之位既正，懿、獻二主，當有所歸。

translations.literal: Once the Grand Ancestor's position is corrected, the two lords of Eminence and Offerings must have a place to go.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Grand Ancestor's seat is corrected, the tablets of Eminence and Offerings must have somewhere to go.

sentences.zh: 詳考十四狀，其意有四：一曰藏諸夾室，二曰置之別廟，三曰遷於園寢，四曰祔於興聖。

translations.literal: Examining the fourteen memorials in detail, their intent has four points: first, store in the side chambers; second, place in a separate temple; third, move to the park tomb; fourth, enshrine in Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the fourteen memorials, their intent has four points: store in side chambers; place in a separate temple; move to the park tomb; or enshrine in Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 藏諸夾室，是無饗獻之期，異乎周人藏於二祧之義，禮不可行也。

translations.literal: Storing in side chambers means no term for offering and presentation—unlike the Zhou practice of storing in the two remote temples; ritual cannot be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Storing in side chambers means no scheduled offerings—unlike the Zhou practice of the two remote temples; ritual cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 置之別廟，始于魏明之說，實非《禮經》之文。

translations.literal: Placing in a separate temple began with Wei Ming's proposal; it is truly not text of the Ritual Classics.
translations.idiomatic: A separate temple began with Wei Ming's proposal; it is not in the Ritual Classics.

sentences.zh: 晉，雖立此義，已後亦無行者。

translations.literal: Jin, though it established this meaning, thereafter also had no practitioners.
translations.idiomatic: Jin established this idea, but thereafter no one practiced it.

sentences.zh: 遷於園寢，是亂宗廟之儀，既無所憑，殊乖經意，不足徵也。

translations.literal: Moving to the park tomb disarranges ancestral-temple observance; having nothing to rely on, it greatly departs from classic intent and is insufficient as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Moving to the park tomb disrupts ancestral-temple observance, has no authority, and greatly departs from the classics—it cannot be cited.

sentences.zh: 惟有祔於興聖之廟，禘祫之歲乃一祭之，庶乎亡於禮者之禮，而得變之正也。

translations.literal: Only enshrining in the temple of Xingsheng, offering once in the years of di and xia—roughly the ritual of what was lost in ritual, obtaining the correction of change.
translations.idiomatic: Only enshrining in the Xingsheng temple and offering once in di and xia years—roughly the rite for what ritual has lost, obtaining the proper change.

translations.literal: The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ended.

sentences.zh: 十九年三月，給事中陳京奏：「禘是大合祖宗之祭，必尊太祖之位，以正昭穆。

translations.literal: Third month of the nineteenth year, Supervising Secretary Chen Jing memorialized: "Di is the great joint sacrifice to ancestors and forbears; the Grand Ancestor's position must be honored to correct zhao-mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the nineteenth year, Supervising Secretary Chen Jing memorialized: "Di is the great joint sacrifice to ancestors; the Grand Ancestor's seat must be honored to correct zhao-mu.

sentences.zh: 今年遇禘，伏恐須定向來所議之禮。

translations.literal: This year encountering di, we fear it will be necessary to fix direction according to the deliberation hitherto.
translations.idiomatic: This year a di is due; we fear the rites must follow the deliberation to date.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「」時左僕射姚南仲等獻議狀五十七封，詔付都省再集百僚議定聞奏。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "" At that time Left Vice Director Yao Nanzong and others submitted fifty-seven memorials; an edict ordered the Chief Secretariat again to assemble all officials, fix by deliberation, and report.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict said: "" At that time Left Vice Director Yao Nanzong and others submitted fifty-seven memorials; an edict ordered the Chief Secretariat again to assemble all officials, decide by deliberation, and report.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書王紹等五十五人奏議：「請奉遷獻祖、懿祖神主祔德明、興聖廟，請別增兩室奉安神主。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wang Shao and fifty-five others memorialized in deliberation: "We ask to move and enshrine the spirit tablets of Xianzu and Yizu in the temples of Deming and Xingsheng, and separately add two chambers to install the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Wang Shao and fifty-five others memorialized: "We ask to move the tablets of Xianzu and Yizu to the Deming and Xingsheng temples and separately add two chambers for the tablets.

sentences.zh: 緣二十四日禘祭，修廟未成，請於德明、興聖廟垣內權設幕屋為二室，暫安神主。

translations.literal: Because on the twenty-fourth the di sacrifice is held and temple repair is not finished, we ask within the walls of the Deming and Xingsheng temples temporarily to set up curtain-houses as two chambers and temporarily install the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Because di falls on the twenty-fourth and temple repair is unfinished, we ask to set up temporary curtain-houses as two chambers within the Deming and Xingsheng temple compounds and temporarily install the tablets.

sentences.zh: 候增修廟室成，准禮遷祔神主入新廟。

translations.literal: When the added and repaired temple chambers are finished, per ritual move and enshrine the spirit tablets into the new temples.
translations.idiomatic: When the new chambers are finished, move the tablets into them per ritual.

sentences.zh: 每至禘祫年，各於本室行饗禮。

translations.literal: Each year of di and xia, perform offering rites in their respective chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In each di and xia year, perform offerings in their respective chambers.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 是月十五日，遷獻祖、懿祖神主權祔德明、興聖廟之幕殿。

translations.literal: Fifteenth day of that month, the spirit tablets of Xianzu and Yizu were moved and temporarily enshrined in the curtain-halls of the Deming and Xingsheng temples.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of that month, the tablets of Xianzu and Yizu were moved and temporarily enshrined in the curtain-halls of the Deming and Xingsheng temples.

sentences.zh: 二十四日，饗太廟。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth day, offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth, offerings were made at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自此景皇帝始居東向之尊，元皇帝已下依左昭右穆之列矣。

translations.literal: From this point Emperor Jing began to occupy the east-facing honor; from Emperor Yuan downward they followed the left-zhao right-mu array.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Emperor Jing took the east-facing honor; from Emperor Yuan downward they followed left-zhao right-mu.

sentences.zh: 二祖新廟成，敕曰：「」又詔曰：「」

translations.literal: When the two ancestors' new temples were completed, an edict said: "" Also an imperial pronouncement said: ""
translations.idiomatic: When the two ancestors' new temples were finished, an edict was issued; an imperial pronouncement followed.

sentences.zh: 十月，太常禮院奏：「禘祫祝文稱號，穆宗皇帝、宣懿皇后韋氏、敬宗皇帝、文宗皇帝、武宗皇帝，緣從前序親親，以穆宗皇帝室稱為皇兄，未合禮文。

translations.literal: Tenth month, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office memorialized: "In di and xia prayer texts, the titles Emperor Muzong, Empress Xuande of the Wei clan, Emperor Jingzong, Emperor Wenzong, and Emperor Wuzong—because of former ordering by near kin, Muzong's chamber was called 'elder brother emperor,' which does not match ritual text.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Ritual Office memorialized: "In di and xia prayer texts, Emperor Muzong, Empress Xuande Wei, Emperor Jingzong, Emperor Wenzong, and Emperor Wuzong—because of former ordering by near kin, Muzong's chamber was called 'elder brother emperor,' which does not match ritual text.

sentences.zh: 得修撰官朱儔等狀稱：『禮敘尊尊，不敘親親。

translations.literal: The memorial of Compiler Zhu Chou and others stated: "'Ritual orders honor to honor, not kin to kin.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Zhu Chou and others reported: "'Ritual orders honor to honor, not kin to kin.

sentences.zh: 陛下于穆宗、敬宗、武宗三室祝文，恐須但稱嗣皇帝臣某昭告于某宗。

translations.literal: For Your Majesty's prayer texts to the three chambers of Muzong, Jingzong, and Wuzong, we fear it is necessary only to say "the succeeding emperor, your subject so-and-so, announces to such-and-such an ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty's prayer texts to the three chambers of Muzong, Jingzong, and Wuzong, we fear they should say only "the succeeding emperor, your subject so-and-so, announces to such-and-such an ancestor."

sentences.zh: 』臣等同考禮經，於義為允。

translations.literal: ' We and others together examined the ritual classics; in meaning it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: ' We together examined the ritual classics; in meaning this is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: ，祫祭太廟。

translations.literal: —the xia sacrifice was offered at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: —and xia was offered at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 近例，祫祭及親拜郊，皆令中使一人引伐國寶至壇所，所以昭示武功。

translations.literal: Recent precedent: at xia sacrifice and when the ruler personally worships at the suburban altar, one palace envoy was always ordered to lead the captured-state treasure to the altar place, thereby to display martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Recent precedent: at xia sacrifice and when the ruler personally worshipped at the suburban altar, one palace envoy was ordered to lead the captured-state treasure to the altar to display martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 至是上以伐國大事，中使引之非宜，乃令禮官一人，就內庫監領至太廟焉。

translations.literal: On this occasion, because subjugating the state was a great affair, for a palace envoy to lead it was not fitting; therefore one ritual officer was ordered to take charge at the inner storehouse and escort it to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, because subjugating a state was a great affair, a palace envoy leading it was improper; one ritual officer was ordered to take charge at the inner storehouse and escort it to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，高祖之廟，則開府儀同三司淮安王神通、禮部尚書河間王孝恭、陝東道大行台右僕射鄖國公殷開山、吏部尚書渝國公劉政會配饗。

translations.literal: Former observance: at Gaozu's temple, Prince of Huai'an Wang Tong, Minister of Rites Prince of Hejian Wang Xiaogong, Right Vice Director of the Grand Secretariat in Shandong Circuit Duke of E Yin Kaishan, and Minister of Personnel Duke of Yu Liu Zhenghui received complementary sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Former observance: at Gaozu's temple, Prince of Huai'an Wang Tong, Minister of Rites Prince of Hejian Wang Xiaogong, Right Vice Director of the Shandong Grand Secretariat Duke of E Yin Kaishan, and Minister of Personnel Duke of Yu Liu Zhenghui received complementary sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太宗之廟，則司空梁國公房玄齡、尚書右僕射萊國公杜如晦、尚書左僕射申國公高士廉配饗。

translations.literal: At Taizong's temple, Minister of Works Duke of Liang Fang Xuanling, Right Vice Director Duke of Lai Du Ruhui, and Left Vice Director Duke of Shen Gao Shilian received complementary sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's temple, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Gao Shilian received complementary sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 高宗之廟，則司空英國公李勣、尚書左僕射北平縣公張行成、中書令高唐縣公馬周配饗。

translations.literal: For Gaozong's temple chamber: Minister of Works, Duke of Ying, Li Ji; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Duke of Beiping, Zhang Xingcheng; and Secretariat Director, Duke of Gaotang, Ma Zhou shared sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's shrine: Li Ji, Zhang Xingcheng, and Ma Zhou shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 中宗之廟，則侍中平陽郡王敬暉、侍中扶陽郡王桓彥范、中書令南陽郡王袁恕己配享。

translations.literal: For Zhongzong's temple chamber: Palace Attendant, Prince of Pingyang, Jing Hui; Palace Attendant, Prince of Fuyang, Huan Yanfan; and Secretariat Director, Prince of Nanyang, Yuan Shuji shared sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongzong's shrine: Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 睿宗之廟，則太子太傅許國公蘇瑰、尚書左丞相徐國公劉幽求配饗。

translations.literal: For Ruizong's temple chamber: Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Duke of Xu, Su Gui; and Left Chancellor, Duke of Xu, Liu Youqiu shared sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's shrine: Su Gui and Liu Youqiu shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 正月，詔：京城章懷、節湣、惠莊、惠文、惠宣太子，與隱太子、懿德太子同為一廟，呼為七太子廟，以便於祀享。

translations.literal: In the first month, an edict stated: In the capital, Crown Princes Zhanghuai, Jiemin, Huizhuang, Huiwen, and Huixuan, together with the Hidden Crown Prince and Crown Princess Yide, were united in one temple, called the Seven Crown Princes' Temple, for convenience in sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: First month, edict: Zhanghuai, Jiemin, Huizhuang, Huiwen, and Huixuan were united with the Hidden Crown Prince and Yide in one shrine, the Seven Crown Princes' Temple, for easier offerings.

sentences.zh: 太廟配饗功臣，高祖室加裴寂、劉文靜，太宗室加長孫無忌、李靖、杜如晦，高宗室加褚遂良、高季輔、劉仁軌，中宗室加狄仁傑、魏元忠、王同皎等十一人。

translations.literal: At the Grand Temple, meritorious ministers sharing sacrifice: to Gaozu's chamber were added Pei Ji and Liu Wenjing; to Taizong's, Zhangsun Wuji, Li Jing, and Du Ruhui; to Gaozong's, Chu Suiliang, Gao Jifu, and Liu Rengui; to Zhongzong's, Di Renjie, Wei Yuanzhong, Wang Tongjiao, and eleven others in all.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Temple merit-sharing was expanded: Pei Ji and Liu Wenjing for Gaozu; Zhangsun Wuji, Li Jing, and Du Ruhui for Taizong; Chu Suiliang, Gao Jifu, and Liu Rengui for Gaozong; Di Renjie, Wei Yuanzhong, Wang Tongjiao, and eight others for Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀，騂犢減數。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices, red bullocks were reduced in number.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices used fewer red bullocks.

sentences.zh: 十載，太廟置內官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, inner palace officials were installed at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, inner-palace officers were assigned to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 十一載閏三月，制：「」其後又有玄宗子靜德太子廟，肅宗子恭懿太子廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, intercalary third month, a regulation stated: "From this time forward, on the first and fifteenth of each month, the Imperial Kitchen shall prepare food and offer it to the Grand Temple; each chamber one tooth-pattern platter; inner palace officials shall present the offerings. Furthermore, every five days the chamber doors shall be opened for sweeping." Thereafter there were also temples to Xuanzong's son the Jingde Crown Prince and to Suzong's son the Gongyi Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh year, intercalary third month: monthly offerings on the first and fifteenth were ordered—Imperial Kitchen food, one platter per chamber, presented by inner-palace officers; chamber doors opened every five days for sweeping. Later came shrines to Xuanzong's son Jingde and Suzong's son Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 孝敬廟在東京太廟院內，貞順皇后、讓皇帝廟在京中。

translations.literal: The Xiaojing Temple was within the Eastern Capital Grand Temple compound; the temples of Empress Zhenshun and Emperor Rang were in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaojing shrine stood in the Eastern Capital temple precinct; Empress Zhenshun and Emperor Rang had shrines in the capital.

sentences.zh: 餘皆四時致祭。

translations.literal: The rest all received offerings at the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: All others received seasonal offerings.
